newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada union urges rejection of Inco offer.
newsitem.headline: Canada union urges rejection of Inco offer.

text.p: The union representing workers at Inco Ltd's division in Thompson, Manitoba, said on Saturday that it told its members to reject Inco's final offer.
The 1,327 workers represented by the union will vote on the company's offer on Sunday, said Bob Desjarlai, president of Local 6166 of the United Steelworkers of America.
"The (union) executive and the negotiating committee are unanimously recommending that our members reject the final offer," Desjarlai said in a telephone interview.
The union's current three-year contract expires at midnight on Sunday, September 15.
If no agreement is reached by that time, union members are in a position to strike.
The main issues in the talks are pensions, wages, benefits and health and safety, the union said earlier.
Inco spokesman Mark Tessier confirmed on Saturday that the company had made its final offer.
"We believe the offer is fair and responsible, and we hope it will be accepted when the membership votes on it tommorrow (Sunday)," Tessier said.
Inco's Thompson operations produce about 100 million pounds of nickel a year in northern Manitoba.
